canonical_definition: Based on the provided data, Test-time scaling is defined as the degree to which a model's performance improves with increased computational effort at inference time. This additional effort is operationalized through mechanisms such as using more iterations or samples. For example, one paper observes that "the performance gain of our approach becomes more pronounced with increasing iterations of MCTS" (VReST: Enhancing Reasoning in Large Vision-Language Models through Tree Search and Self-Reward Mechanism). The construct is framed as a reflection of the "efficiency of reasoning refinement." The available source material consistently discusses this concept in the context of multimodal tasks, with one paper noting that a method "exhibits a better test-time scaling law on multimodal reasoning tasks".
